chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Jameela al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Muhammad al-Halbi, and Zurara, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And remember your Lord when you forget.' He said: 'When a man swears and forgets to make a condition (Insha-Allah), let him make the condition when he remembers.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets to say Insha-Allah while making an oath?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the practical application of Surah Al-Kahf 18:24, establishing that forgetting to include 'Insha-Allah' in an oath does not invalidate it but requires immediate rectification upon remembrance. Shia jurists cite this to emphasize that human actions are contingent upon Divine Will, thereby preserving the oath's validity while acknowledging God's sovereignty over future events.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Jameela Al Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Muhammad Al Halby, and Zurara, and Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [18:24] and remember your Lord when you forget. When the man swears, so he forgets (to say ‘Allahazwj Willing’ (Insha-Allahazwj), so let him say it when he remembers’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu Jamilah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Muhammad al-Halabiy and Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following:

“About the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, . . speak of your Lord if you forget’ [18:24] abu Ja‘far, and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, have said that if one takes an oath and forgets to make an exception, he must make an exception (say, ‘if Allah wills’) when he remembers.”
